title: Other whites to know
subtitle: Five grapes that matter
objectives: Name a classic region for each grape

steps.title: Grüner Veltliner and Assyrtiko
steps.body: Grüner Veltliner is Austria's signature grape: crisp, with citrus, green apple and white pepper, from light to powerful in the Wachau. Assyrtiko, from Santorini in Greece, keeps very high acidity even in hot sun, and grows on volcanic soil, giving firm, mineral, citrus wines.
steps.highlight: Grüner: white pepper. Assyrtiko: acid and volcanic.

steps.title: Muscat and Torrontés
steps.body: Muscat is a family of grapes that tastes like fresh grapes, thanks to terpenes like linalool and geraniol. It makes light, sweet Moscato d'Asti at 5.5% and rich, fortified wines in southern France. Torrontés, Argentina's white grape, a cross that includes Muscat of Alexandria, gives floral wines in high Salta, up to 3,000 m.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its home.
steps.explanation: Each grape has a region where it shows best.

steps.title: Melon and Garganega
steps.body: Melon de Bourgogne makes Muscadet, near the Loire's mouth: light, crisp and often aged on its lees, labelled sur lie, which adds texture and a slight spritz. Garganega is the main grape of Soave, in the Veneto, giving almond, lemon and a light texture, and sweet Recioto di Soave from dried grapes.
steps.highlight: Muscadet sur lie; Soave from Garganega

steps.prompt: Muscadet is made from the Muscat grape.
steps.explanation: Not true. Despite the name, Muscadet is made from Melon de Bourgogne. Muscat is a different, aromatic family.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Grüner Veltliner and Assyrtiko are crisp, high-acid whites
Muscat and Torrontés are floral, grape-scented whites
Muscadet comes from Melon; Soave from Garganega
